title: file sink pending-write queue is unbounded: records pile up in memory without limit when appendFile is slow or never settles
area: packages/ai/src/trace-file-sink.ts record(): tail = tail.then(() => append(line)).catch(() => undefined) (no pending cap, no drop-when-full); reachable on every routed model call once TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true and TELEMETRY_TRACE_FILE is set
evidence: Probe: stub fs/promises appendFile to return a never-settling promise, fileSink({path, warn(){}}), call sink.record(rec) 100000 times, gc, measure heapUsed: +63.2 MiB, stats.written 0, dropped 0 (linear, about 660 B/record). Size guard and failure counters do not engage because the pending append never resolves or is merely slow.
fix_direction: Count pending records; above a cap (for example 1000) drop new records, increment stats.dropped and warn once. Add a test with a never-resolving appendFile asserting dropped > 0 and a bounded pending count.
reproduction: node --expose-gc --import tsx probe: fsp.appendFile = () => new Promise(() => {}); module.syncBuiltinESMExports(); const s = fileSink({path: 'x.jsonl', warn() {}}); for (i < 100000) s.record(rec(i)); gc(); heap growth 63.2 MiB
